newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian rebels said ready for troop handover.
newsitem.headline: Colombian rebels said ready for troop handover.

text.p: Leftist rebel commanders say everything is ready for the handover of at least 60 soldiers they took prisoner in southern Colombia a month ago, a politician acting as mediator in the crisis said on Wednesday.

Ex-senator Alvaro Leyva spoke on his return from a series of secret meetings with the local chieftains and the supreme commander of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) in the jungle region of Putumayo and Caqueta provinces.

The troops were seized on Aug. 30 after rebels overran their base in Las Delicias, in Putumayo province, killing 27. The attack marked the start of one of the bloodiest guerrilla offensives in decades.

"I was with regional commanders and with the commander-in- chief Manuel Marulanda (alias "Sureshot"). I don't think there are any problems and all the conditions are in place. Let's hope the release is soon," Leyva told reporters in Bogota.
No date for the release of the prisoners of war has yet been set, but in a communique earlier this week the FARC called for the demilitarization of three zones in Caqueta province.
President Ernesto Samper agreed on Tuesday that international observers would be allowed to witness the handover, thus removing one of the final obstacles to the soldiers' release.

The rebels were insisting on the presence of international delegates in the mediation committee to ensure that the military would not try to rescue the troops by force. The government fears the FARC, which has grown rich through kidnapping and banditry, was using the crisis as an opportunity to add an international dimension to its three-decade insurgency.
